user.title: Connect BamBuddy
user.description: Home Assistant reads your printers through your BamBuddy server and sends your commands to it.

data_description.url: The address you open BamBuddy with in your browser, for example `192.168.1.20:8000` or `{example_url}`.
data_description.api_key: Create one in BamBuddy under Settings → API Keys, with all three permissions: Read Status, Control Printer and Manage Maintenance.
data_description.verify_ssl: Only matters for https addresses. Turn it off if BamBuddy uses a self-signed certificate.

printers.title: Choose printers
printers.description: These printers are set up in BamBuddy. Each selected printer becomes a device in Home Assistant. You can add or remove printers later with Configure. Names come from BamBuddy: rename a printer there.

reauth_confirm.title: New BamBuddy API key needed
reauth_confirm.description:
BamBuddy at {url} no longer accepts the stored API key: it was deleted, has expired or was turned off. Your devices, entities and their history are kept.

To create a new API key:

1. In BamBuddy, open Settings → API Keys and choose “Create Key”.
2. Give it a name, such as “Home Assistant”, and tick Read Status, Control Printer and Manage Maintenance.
3. Copy the key and paste it below. BamBuddy shows it only once.

data_description.api_key: Leave it empty to check the stored key again — after a change in BamBuddy, such as a right given to its owner.

reauth_scopes.title: New BamBuddy API key needed

data_description.api_key: Leave it empty to check the stored key again — after a change in BamBuddy, such as a right given to its owner.

reauth_owner.title: New BamBuddy API key needed
reauth_owner.description:
BamBuddy at {url} knows the stored API key, but its owner is deactivated or deleted in BamBuddy. Your devices, entities and their history are kept.

To create a new API key:

1. Sign in to BamBuddy as an active user, open Settings → API Keys and choose “Create Key”.
2. Give it a name, such as “Home Assistant”, and tick Read Status, Control Printer and Manage Maintenance.
3. Copy the key and paste it below. BamBuddy shows it only once.

data_description.api_key: Leave it empty to check the stored key again — after a change in BamBuddy, such as a right given to its owner.

reconfigure.title: Change the connection
reconfigure.description: Change the address or the API key of your BamBuddy server. At a new address you choose next which printers stay.

data_description.url: The address you open BamBuddy with in your browser, for example `192.168.1.20:8000` or `{example_url}`.
data_description.api_key: Leave it empty to keep the current key. A new one needs all three permissions: Read Status, Control Printer and Manage Maintenance.
data_description.verify_ssl: Only matters for https addresses. Turn it off if BamBuddy uses a self-signed certificate.

new_address.title: New address
new_address.description:
BamBuddy answers at {url}. These printers were found there by their serial numbers and keep their devices and history:

{kept}

data.remove_printers: Remove printers not in this BamBuddy

data_description.remove_printers: Ticked ones leave Home Assistant with their AMS units and smart plugs. Unticked ones stay and wait under Settings → Repairs until BamBuddy lists them again.
data_description.add_printers: Each becomes a device in Home Assistant.

new_address_all.title: New address
new_address_all.description: BamBuddy answers at {url}. Every printer of this entry was found there by its serial number and keeps its device and history.

data_description.add_printers: Each becomes a device in Home Assistant.

other_bambuddy.title: Another BamBuddy?
other_bambuddy.description: None of this entry's printers is set up in the BamBuddy at {url}. Is it another BamBuddy, or the same one before its printers are set up there again? For another BamBuddy, tick its old printers below to remove them.

data.remove_printers: Remove printers not in this BamBuddy

data_description.remove_printers: Ticked ones leave Home Assistant with their AMS units and smart plugs. Unticked ones stay and wait under Settings → Repairs until BamBuddy lists them again.
data_description.add_printers: Each becomes a device in Home Assistant.

new_address_no_printers.title: New address
new_address_no_printers.description: BamBuddy answers at {url}. This entry has no printers yet.

data_description.add_printers: Each becomes a device in Home Assistant.

error.cannot_connect: BamBuddy does not answer at this address, or this is not BamBuddy's address. Check the address including the port (usually 8000) and that BamBuddy is running.
error.invalid_auth: BamBuddy does not accept this API key. Check that you pasted all of it. BamBuddy shows a key only once: if you no longer have it, create a new one.
error.missing_scopes: The API key you entered lacks permissions: Read Status {read_status}, Control Printer {control_printer}, Manage Maintenance {manage_maintenance}. BamBuddy cannot add permissions to an existing key: create a new one with all three. If you ticked one marked ✗ in BamBuddy, the key's owner may not do it: give them that right, or create the key as a user who has it.
error.key_owner_inactive: BamBuddy knows this API key, but its owner is deactivated or deleted. Sign in to BamBuddy as an active user and create a new key with Read Status, Control Printer and Manage Maintenance.
error.bambuddy_refused: BamBuddy refused a read although the API key has every permission the integration needs: {error}
error.stored_key_refused: BamBuddy no longer accepts the stored API key. Enter a new one.
error.stored_key_scopes: The stored API key lacks permissions: Read Status {read_status}, Control Printer {control_printer}, Manage Maintenance {manage_maintenance}. Enter a new one with all three.
error.stored_key_owner: The stored API key's owner is deactivated or deleted in BamBuddy. Enter a new one, created as an active user.
error.invalid_url: This is not a valid address. Enter it like 192.168.1.20:8000 or {example_url}.
error.not_bambuddy: No BamBuddy answers at this address, or it is older than version {minimum}.
error.too_old: BamBuddy {version} is too old. Update BamBuddy to version {minimum} or newer.
error.ssl_error: BamBuddy's certificate could not be verified. If BamBuddy uses a self-signed certificate, turn off “Verify SSL certificate”.
error.url_with_login: Leave the user name and password out of the address: the integration signs in with the API key.
error.address_in_use: This address already belongs to another BamBuddy entry.
error.not_https: BamBuddy does not use https at this address. Enter it with http://, such as http://192.168.1.20:8000.
error.error_not_bambuddy: This address answered with an error ({error}). Is it BamBuddy's address?

abort.already_configured:
This BamBuddy server is already set up.

To add or remove its printers, use “Configure” on its entry.
abort.address_in_use: This address already belongs to another BamBuddy entry. Nothing was changed.
abort.reauth_successful: The API key works. BamBuddy is connected again.
abort.reconfigure_successful_missing: The connection has been changed. Not found: {printers}. You can remove them under Settings → Repairs, or all at once with Configure → Remove printers.
abort.reconfigure_successful_other: The connection has been changed. The BamBuddy device's history starts afresh.
abort.reconfigure_successful_other_missing: The connection has been changed. The BamBuddy device's history starts afresh. Not found: {printers}. You can remove them under Settings → Repairs, or all at once with Configure → Remove printers.
abort.printers_in_use: Every printer of this BamBuddy is set up already, through {entries}. To reach BamBuddy at another address, use ⋮ → Reconfigure on that entry; to add or remove printers, use “Configure” there.

create_entry.no_printers: BamBuddy has no printers yet: the integration starts with BamBuddy's own figures. Once a printer is set up in BamBuddy, add it here under Configure → Add printers.

init.title: Manage printers
init.description: Add printers of “{name}” to Home Assistant or remove them.

add_printer.title: Add printers
add_printer.description: These printers are set up in “{name}” but not yet in Home Assistant.

remove_printer.title: Remove printers
remove_printer.description: The selected printers of “{name}” leave Home Assistant with their AMS units, smart plugs and entities. Nothing changes in BamBuddy. “Add printers” brings them back later.

abort.cannot_connect: “{name}” cannot be reached. Try again later.
abort.no_printers: “{name}” has no printers yet. Set one up in BamBuddy first, then add it here.
abort.all_printers_added: Every printer of “{name}” is added already.
abort.key_refused: “{name}” no longer accepts the API key. Enter a new one where Home Assistant asks for it, under Settings → Devices & services.
abort.printers_in_use: BamBuddy's printers that this entry lacks are set up through {entries} already.

auto_off_temperature.name: Switch off when nozzle is below

bambuddy_too_old.message: BamBuddy {version} is too old for this integration. Update BamBuddy to version {minimum} or newer.

auth_failed.message: BamBuddy no longer accepts the API key. Enter a new one under Settings → Repairs.

key_doubted.message: BamBuddy refused the API key; it is checked again within a minute.

key_scopes_missing.message: The API key lacks permissions the integration needs (Read Status {read_status}, Control Printer {control_printer}, Manage Maintenance {manage_maintenance}). Enter a new key under Settings → Repairs.

key_owner_inactive.message: The API key's owner is deactivated or deleted in BamBuddy. Sign in to BamBuddy as an active user, create a key with Read Status, Control Printer and Manage Maintenance, and enter it under Settings → Repairs.

key_check_unreadable.message: BamBuddy's answer about the API key names no permissions. Update the integration, or report it.

update_failed.message: BamBuddy cannot be reached. Is the BamBuddy server running, and is the address right? ({error})

cannot_connect.message: BamBuddy cannot be reached. Check that it is running.

cannot_delete_instance.message: The BamBuddy server itself cannot be deleted here. To remove it, delete the BamBuddy integration entry.

cannot_delete_ams.message: Its printer still reports this AMS unit. Unplug it first; then its device can be deleted.

printer_replaced.message: BamBuddy now lists another printer under the number of {printer}. The integration reloads to find {printer} again by its serial number.

job_running.message: {printer} is printing or paused: this works once the print is done or stopped.

plate_not_waiting.message: {printer} is not waiting for the plate to be cleared.

not_a_printer.message: Choose a printer of a loaded BamBuddy integration (not an AMS unit, a smart plug or BamBuddy itself).

not_an_ams.message: Choose an AMS unit of a loaded BamBuddy integration (not a printer, a smart plug or BamBuddy itself).

not_a_slot.message: Choose an AMS slot or an external spool of a loaded BamBuddy integration.

ams_ht_load.message: BamBuddy cannot load filament from an AMS HT. Load it on the printer itself.

load_track_switch.message: {printer} feeds its nozzles through the Filament Track Switch, so a load has to say which nozzle to feed. Load the filament on the printer or in BamBuddy.

nozzle_too_cold.message: The nozzle is at {temperature} °C. Heat it to at least {minimum} °C before extruding.

filament_change.message: {printer} is changing filament. Wait until it is done.

pause_first.message: {printer} is printing. Pause the print to change the filament.

rfid_spool.message: This spool's chip tells the printer its filament; it cannot be set by hand. If the spool has no chip, the printer may still remember the last one: take the spool out until the slot shows empty, then put it back.

slot_in_use.message: {printer} is printing from this slot. Pause the print to change its filament.

material_needed.message: The printer knows no material for this slot yet: choose one.

nothing_to_set.message: Choose at least one of material, color and K profile.

no_answer.message: BamBuddy did not answer in time; the command may still reach the printer. Check that BamBuddy is running and not overloaded.

cannot_dry.message: This AMS unit cannot dry filament. The AMS 2 Pro and the AMS HT can.

already_drying.message: This AMS unit is drying already: stop the drying first to start another.

not_drying.message: This AMS unit is not drying.

drying_parked.message: The printer still counts this AMS unit as drying, but its countdown stands still. Stop the drying on the printer or in BamBuddy, then start it again.

dry_while_printing.message: {printer} cannot dry while it prints. Start the drying once the print is done.

dry_on_screen.message: {printer} starts drying only from its own screen.

dry_firmware.message: The firmware of {printer} cannot start drying from here. Update the printer.

update_timeout.message: BamBuddy did not answer in time. Check that it is running and not overloaded. ({error})

printer_not_listed.message: BamBuddy does not list {printer} right now. Settings → Repairs says what to do.

ams_not_reported.message: {printer} does not report this AMS unit right now. Is it plugged in?

dry_stop_on_screen.message: {printer} stops drying only from its own screen.

plug_not_answering.message: The smart plug {plug} does not answer BamBuddy. Check that it is plugged in and on the network.

plug_command_failed.message: BamBuddy could not switch the smart plug {plug}: {error}

auto_off_bambuddy.message: BamBuddy already switches the plug {plug} off after the print (its Auto Off). Turn that off in BamBuddy to use it here.

cannot_delete_plug.message: BamBuddy still links this smart plug to the printer, so its device would come back. Unlink or delete the plug in BamBuddy: its device then goes by itself within a minute.

hms_not_current.message: The printer does not report the HMS message {code} now.

hms_answer_not_offered.message: The printer does not offer this answer for the HMS message {code}.

hms_answer_screen_only.message: This answer only works on the printer's own screen; Home Assistant cannot send it.

k_profile_unknown.message: {printer} has no K profile with this index for the nozzle that feeds the slot.

rfid_not_external.message: The external spools have no chip reader.

rfid_unload_first.message: Unload the filament first: the AMS of {printer} reads a chip only while no filament is loaded.

k_profiles_no_answer.message: {printer} did not list its K profiles. Ask again in a moment: a printer may not answer twice in a row.

slot_pause_first.message: {printer} is printing. Pause the print first.

hms_answer_not_taken.message: {printer} did not take the answer. Is it still connected to BamBuddy?

confirm.title: Remove the printer?
confirm.description: BamBuddy no longer lists the printer {printer}. If it was removed in BamBuddy on purpose, choose “Remove printer” to remove it here too: the printer, its AMS units, its smart plugs and their entities leave Home Assistant, nothing changes in BamBuddy. If it is back in BamBuddy, close this: it comes back here by itself within a minute.

abort.already_removed: The printer has been removed already.

names_from_bambuddy.title: Names come from BamBuddy: {name}
names_from_bambuddy.description:
You renamed devices of this printer in Home Assistant:

- {given}

Their names come from BamBuddy and went back to BamBuddy's.

Rename the printer in BamBuddy instead: Home Assistant follows within seconds (an AMS unit is named after its printer).

confirm.title: AMS entity IDs renamed

abort.already_confirmed: This notice has been confirmed already.

create_entry.default: The notice is closed. Each unit's device page lists its entity IDs.

move_axis.name: Move axis
move_axis.description: Moves the toolhead or the bed by a distance. Not possible while a print is running or paused.

axis.name: Axis
axis.description: X and Y move the toolhead (on the A1, the A1 mini and the A2L, Y moves the bed); Z changes the distance between nozzle and bed.

distance.name: Distance
distance.description: In millimeters; negative values move the other way. For Z, a positive distance moves nozzle and bed apart.

home_axes.name: Home axes
home_axes.description: Moves all axes to their home position. Remove any object from the plate first. Not possible while a print is running or paused.

extrude.name: Extrude
extrude.description: Pushes filament through the nozzle, or pulls it back. The nozzle must be hot. Not possible while a print is running or paused.

distance.name: Length
distance.description: In millimeters; a negative length retracts the filament.

load_filament.name: Load filament
load_filament.description: Loads the filament of an AMS slot or of the external spool into the nozzle (not from an AMS HT: BamBuddy cannot; and not from an AMS slot of a printer with the Filament Track Switch: such a load must name the nozzle — load it on the printer or in BamBuddy). While a print is running, pause it first.

entity_id.name: Slot
entity_id.description: The sensor of the AMS slot or of the external spool.

unload_filament.name: Unload filament
unload_filament.description: Pulls the loaded filament out of the nozzle — on a two-nozzle printer, out of the active one. While a print is running, pause it first.

start_drying.name: Start drying
start_drying.description: Dries the filament in an AMS unit that can dry, like the AMS 2 Pro or the AMS HT.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Drying temperature; the AMS 2 Pro reaches at most 65 °C.

stop_drying.name: Stop drying
stop_drying.description: Stops drying in an AMS unit.

device_id.name: AMS unit
device_id.description: The AMS unit that stops drying.

get_print_objects.name: Get print objects
get_print_objects.description: Lists the objects of the running print with their IDs, and which are skipped already.

skip_objects.name: Skip objects
skip_objects.description: Leaves objects out of the rest of the running print, for example one that came off the plate. This cannot be undone.

objects.name: Objects
objects.description: The IDs of the objects, as Get print objects lists them.

set_filament.name: Set filament
set_filament.description: Sets the material and color of an AMS slot or of the external spool, as the printer asks after a spool without a chip goes in. A new color keeps the slot's profile; a new material takes Bambu's generic profile and the default flow dynamics (K) value. Not for Bambu spools with a chip: the printer reads those itself.

entity_id.name: Slot
entity_id.description: The sensor of the AMS slot or of the external spool, for example "… Slot 2" or "… External spool".

material.name: Material
material.description: Leave empty to keep the slot's material.

color.name: Color
color.description: Leave empty to keep the slot's color.

k_profile.name: K profile
k_profile.description: One of the printer's K calibrations by its index, as Get K profiles lists them; -1 is the printer's default K.

run_diagnostic.name: Check connection
run_diagnostic.description: Has BamBuddy check its connection to the printer: its ports, the access code, developer mode, whether it reports. Sends the printer no command; takes a few seconds, at most half a minute.

mark_maintenance_done.name: Mark maintenance done
mark_maintenance_done.description: Marks a maintenance task of the printer as done in BamBuddy: its count starts over.

device_id.name: Printer
device_id.description: The printer the task belongs to.

task_id.name: Task
task_id.description: The task's ID: the field id of the task in the attribute Tasks of the printer's Maintenance sensor.

answer_hms.name: Answer an HMS message
answer_hms.description: Answers one of the printer's HMS messages as its screen would, for example resume once the filament is loaded. Only an answer the printer offers for the message now; its attribute actions lists them.

code.name: Code
code.description: The message's code, as the HMS sensor's errors attribute lists it, such as 0700_2000_0002_0012.

action.name: Answer
action.description: One of the message's actions, such as RESUME_PRINTING_PROBELM_SOLVED (Bambu's spelling).

get_k_profiles.name: Get K profiles
get_k_profiles.description: Lists the printer's own K (pressure advance) calibrations for the nozzle that feeds a slot, as Set filament takes them, and the slot's current one. The printer is asked live (up to about 16 seconds); an empty list means it listed none or did not answer.

entity_id.name: Slot
entity_id.description: The sensor of the slot (or of the external spool).

reset_slot.name: Reset slot
reset_slot.description: Clears a slot's material and color, as Reset on the printer's screen; a spool with a chip shows again once the AMS reads it. Not during a running print; in a paused one it is allowed.

entity_id.name: Slot
entity_id.description: The sensor of the slot (or of the external spool).

refresh_rfid.name: Read the chip again
refresh_rfid.description: Lets the AMS read the chip of the spool in a slot again, for a Bambu Lab spool it did not recognize. BamBuddy allows it only while no filament is loaded; the external spools have no reader. Not during a running print; in a paused one it is allowed.

entity_id.name: Slot
entity_id.description: The sensor of the slot (or of the external spool).

options.same: The same BamBuddy at a new address (everything stays, history included)
options.other: Another BamBuddy (the BamBuddy device's figures start afresh and their history is deleted; the printers keep theirs)
